_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: project_appdirect_onboard_oauth_scope_default.md (PR #74, 2026-06-07).

handfixes.summary: APPDIRECT_OAUTH_SCOPE is optional + non-secret (has a working default 'ROLE_PARTNER ROLE_PARTNER_READ'); the press marked it required + sensitive
handfixes.why: client.go/auth.go resolveClientCredentialsScope() returns the working default 'ROLE_PARTNER ROLE_PARTNER_READ' when APPDIRECT_OAUTH_SCOPE is empty and SENDS it (form.Set('scope', ...)), so the scope is not a credential and the user need not supply one. The press emitted required:true / sensitive:true in BOTH manifest.json user_config AND server.json environmentVariables. Fixed to optional + non-secret. This is the OPPOSITE of the halopsa bug (scope wired but never sent -> 401): here scope IS sent with a default. A reprint reverts both to required+secret.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Spec hook: mark OAUTH_SCOPE optional + non-secret in x-auth-env-vars metadata so the press emits required:false / sensitive:false by construction. Always read the binary's scope-resolver before classifying OAUTH_SCOPE.

handfixes.summary: MCP binary renamed appdirect-pp-mcp -> appdirect-mcp in manifest.json (name/entry_point); the press emits the -pp- name
handfixes.why: onboard re-vendors+patches manifest.json from source every run, so the -pp-mcp -> appdirect-mcp rename in name/entry_point must be re-applied after the final --resume. release.yml builds <slug>-mcp from skills.json and doesn't build a .mcpb, so manifest name/entry_point are effectively inert - but renamed anyway to honor the autotask #35 convention. A reprint/re-onboard reverts the name to appdirect-pp-mcp.

handfixes.summary: Governance reclassified method-aware: ~35 verb-less writes promoted out of Read, with explicit Credential (7) and Destructive (34) tiers (DELETE/expire = destructive; payment/password = credential)
handfixes.why: gen_governance missed ~35 verb-less writes (add/apply/change/clone/edit/execute/finalize/remove/request/notify/upload/invite/save/bill-usage/expire) plus appwise events/provisioning -> all fell to Read. Reclassified method-aware from agent-context pp:method (Read 168 / Write 118 / Credential 7 / Destructive 34): all DELETE + expire destructive; payment-method/instrument + password credential; POST-as-query (get-pricing-summary/preview-shopping-cart) stay Read. A reprint regenerates governance.md from the keyword classifier and silently demotes the writes.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Real fix is a method-aware gen_governance (classify from pp:method, not the command-name verb). Tracked in project_gen_governance_misses_verbless_writes / project_governance_rewrite_union_not_replace.

handfixes.summary: Vendor trademark owner stored without a trailing period ('AppDirect, Inc') so the non-affiliation banner doesn't double-period
handfixes.why: Owner 'AppDirect, Inc.' + the template's '.' produced 'Inc..'; the owner is stored without the trailing period (like knowbe4). A reprint with the period-terminated owner string reintroduces the double period.

handfixes.summary: SaveTokens keeps the env-override marker on ClientID/ClientSecret, so env-supplied OAuth credentials are never written to config.toml (issue #266)
handfixes.why: Load() marks ClientID/ClientSecret as env overrides and configForSave() restores the file value for any field still marked -- the mechanism that keeps env-supplied secrets off disk. SaveTokens() cleared both markers on every save, so each token mint (an ordinary authenticated command, no `auth login` step needed) rewrote the live client_id and client_secret into ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext, defeating Keychain/Credential-Manager setups that inject the secret as an env var at process launch. SaveTokens now leaves those two markers alone; only MarkCredentialsExplicit clears them, and only `auth login` calls it, passing whether each value came from a flag rather than from the env fallback. Provenance must be declared, not inferred: comparing the incoming value against the loaded one cannot tell an explicit flag from the env value it duplicates, and `auth login` trims its env fallback while Load does not, so a padded variable compares unequal to itself and leaks. Reported by @Xenith-B against halopsa-cli/ninjaone-cli. GENERATOR-class defect (the press emits the unconditional deletes) tracked for an upstream retro; until the press is fixed, a reprint reintroduces the leak and these markers guard the connector. Bug-fix-only: no new flag, command, or output.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press#4283: SaveTokens must not clear the ClientID/ClientSecret env-override markers. Only a credential the caller supplied through an explicit command-line flag may clear them, and the flag's provenance must be passed in by the caller -- NOT inferred by comparing the incoming value against the loaded one. An explicit flag whose value equals the environment's is still explicit and must persist; conversely `auth login` trims its env fallback while Load does not, so a padded variable compares unequal to itself and a value-based rule leaks it.

asserts.contains: markers now survive a save; only MarkCredentialsExplicit clears them.

handfixes.summary: doctor, the CLI error path and the MCP error path all point at `appdirect-cli auth login` instead of a nonexistent `auth setup` subcommand (issue #277, #278)
handfixes.why: This CLI's `auth` parent defines login, status, set-token and logout. It has never defined `setup`, yet three generated surfaces told operators to run it: doctor.go's auth_hint (fires when cfg.AuthHeader() is empty), helpers.go's HTTP 400/401/403 remediation, and internal/mcp/tools.go's tool-error text -- 7 occurrences in all. Cobra does not error on an unknown subcommand of a NON-root parent (legacyArgs only rejects unknown args for the root), and the generated parent runs parentNoSubcommandRunE, which returns cmd.Help() -- a nil error. So `appdirect-cli auth setup` printed help and exited 0. There was no 'unknown command' error and no non-zero exit anywhere in the journey: an operator saw a success code and was no closer to credentials, and because these are agent-first CLIs with typed exit codes, an agent performing setup read exit 0 as success and carried on unauthenticated. The hint fires exactly when it matters -- fresh install, rotated secret, new machine, expired token. This skill emits no auth_instructions field, so these hints are the only setup guidance it gives. The replacements name the real command and, in doctor, the variables `auth login` actually reads: APPDIRECT_CLIENT_ID and APPDIRECT_CLIENT_SECRET (plus the optional APPDIRECT_OAUTH_SCOPE), taken from the login command's own env fallbacks rather than composed. Reported by @geekbrownbear, who verified halopsa and ninjaone live against an empty config (PR #277) and filed appdirect/crowdstrike as issue #278; the fleet scan that found the other two surfaces and confirmed only these four connectors are affected was done during triage. GENERATOR-class defect: until the press is fixed, a reprint reintroduces all 7 strings and these asserts guard them. Bug-fix-only: no new flag, command, or output field.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press#4315: Derive the auth hint from the subcommand set the connector actually generates instead of the fixed "Run '<cli> auth setup' for credential setup steps." string in internal/generator/generator.go. 52 of 56 connectors do define `auth setup`, which is why the hard-coded string went unnoticed; the four OAuth client-credentials connectors that scaffold `auth login` instead (appdirect, crowdstrike, halopsa, ninjaone) each shipped it 7 times. The same string is emitted into three surfaces -- doctor.go's auth_hint, helpers.go's 400/401/403 remediation, and the MCP server's tool-error text -- so a generator fix must cover all three.

asserts.contains: Set APPDIRECT_CLIENT_ID and APPDIRECT_CLIENT_SECRET (plus APPDIRECT_OAUTH_SCOPE if your account needs a non-default scope), then run 'appdirect-cli auth login' to mint a token.
